ui.positionHint: Point at a marker on the sphere and pull the trigger.
ui.gateHint: Press the button to apply the turn.
ui.timeoutHint: Time to apply the turn. Press the button.
ui.rotateHint: Grab the tip of the vector and turn it the way the arrow points. Let go when it stops.

tasks.prompt: After a quarter turn toward |1⟩, how often will a measurement give 0?
tasks.correct: Yes, 50%. A quarter turn takes the vector from the top of the sphere to the equator, where 0 and 1 are equally likely.
tasks.noPrediction: A quarter turn took the vector from |0⟩ at the top to the equator. There, 0 and 1 are equally likely: 50% each.
tasks.genericIncorrect: It is 50%. The quarter turn brought the vector to the equator, exactly halfway between |0⟩ and |1⟩, so both outcomes are equally likely.

misconceptions.text: It is 50%. The turn did change the state: the vector moved from |0⟩ at the top down to the equator, where 0 and 1 are equally likely.
It is 50%. A quarter turn moves the vector only halfway from |0⟩ to |1⟩, to the equator. Reaching |1⟩ takes a half turn.

tasks.prompt: After a quarter turn about z, where will the vector point?
tasks.correct: Yes, |+i⟩. A quarter turn about z swings the vector a quarter of the way around the equator, from |+⟩ to |+i⟩.
tasks.noPrediction: A quarter turn about z swung the vector a quarter of the way around the equator, from |+⟩ to |+i⟩.
tasks.genericIncorrect: It ends at |+i⟩. A quarter turn about z moves the vector a quarter of the way around the equator, from |+⟩ to |+i⟩.

misconceptions.text: It ends at |+i⟩. Turns follow the right-hand rule: with your thumb along +z, your fingers curl from |+⟩ toward |+i⟩, not toward |−i⟩.
It ends at |+i⟩. A turn about z changes only the angle around the equator, never the height, so the vector cannot move toward |0⟩ or |1⟩.
It ends at |+i⟩. A turn about z leaves |0⟩ and |1⟩ alone because they sit on the z axis, but |+⟩ is on the equator, so it swings around.

tasks.prompt: After H, where will the vector point?
tasks.correct: Yes, |0⟩. H is a half turn about the axis between x and z. It swaps |0⟩ and |+⟩, so it brings |+⟩ back to |0⟩.
tasks.noPrediction: H is a half turn about the axis between x and z. It swaps |0⟩ and |+⟩, so the vector went from |+⟩ back to |0⟩.
tasks.genericIncorrect: It ends at |0⟩. H is a half turn about the axis between x and z. It swaps |0⟩ and |+⟩, so it brings |+⟩ back to |0⟩.

misconceptions.text: It ends at |0⟩. H does not always make a superposition. It is a half turn that swaps |0⟩ and |+⟩, so from |+⟩ it gives |0⟩.
It ends at |0⟩. A superposition can turn back into a definite state: the same H that took |0⟩ to |+⟩ takes |+⟩ back to |0⟩.
It ends at |0⟩. H is not X. X is a half turn about x and swaps |0⟩ and |1⟩. H turns about the axis between x and z and swaps |0⟩ and |+⟩.

tasks.prompt: After a 60° turn toward |1⟩, how often will a measurement give 0?
tasks.correct: Yes, 75%. After a 60° turn the vector is still closer to |0⟩, so 0 comes up 75% of the time, as the measurements showed.
tasks.noPrediction: After a 60° turn the vector is still closer to |0⟩, so 0 comes up 75% of the time, as the measurements showed.
tasks.genericIncorrect: It is 75%. After a 60° turn the vector is still closer to |0⟩ than to |1⟩, so 0 is the more likely outcome, as the measurements showed.

misconceptions.text: It is 75%. Only states on the equator are 50/50. After a 60° turn the vector is still closer to |0⟩, so 0 is more likely.
It is 75%, not 67%. The chance does not fall evenly with the angle. A 60° turn lowers the tip only a quarter of the way down the sphere.
It is 75%. Any tilt away from |0⟩ makes a superposition, not just the equator. After a 60° turn, 1 already comes up 25% of the time.
